definition: Executive attention is a form of attention involved in directing and controlling processing, and evidence in this packet indicates that it supports both conscious and unconscious processing. Here, it is especially linked to temporal attention and to the working-memory manipulation system rather than the maintenance system.

reasons: The definition states that executive attention is “involved in directing and controlling processing,” but the supplied packet only discusses executive attention’s involvement in conscious vs. unconscious processing and its links to temporal attention and working-memory subsystems; it does not define executive attention as directing/controlling processing.

The remainder of the definition (that evidence indicates executive attention supports both conscious and unconscious processing, and that it is linked to temporal attention and the working-memory manipulation system rather than the maintenance system) is consistent with parts of the packet, but the overall definition fails because of the unsupported first claim.
The packet supports a role in unconscious processing, but it does not support the claim that executive attention also supports conscious processing.
The packet does not define executive attention as a form of attention involved in directing and controlling processing.

The packet supports a link to temporal attention and to the working-memory manipulation subsystem rather than the maintenance subsystem, but the definition overstates the packet by presenting these as the defining sense of the term.
